summary: Provisioning hang: lvmetad metadata lock stalls ecryptfs migration after depot NVMe swap
description:
Issue summary:
Provisioning jobs in the depot are intermittently hanging during the OS post-install migration step where ecryptfs home migration runs. Machines recently repaired with NVMe replacements are disproportionately affected.

Impact:
- ~12% of depot images since the NVMe swap batch (2026-02-25) hang for >30 minutes during 'migrate-encrypted-home' step, blocking depot throughput.
- Affected devices fail to proceed to OOBE/AAD join and require manual intervention.

Environment:
- Staging depot (us-east) using our standard unattended image with Ubuntu 22.04 LTS and our provisioning-agent v1.14.
- NVMe replacements deployed during depot RMA batch 2026-02-24 to 2026-02-26.

Steps to reproduce (observed in depot):
1) Replace primary NVMe with vendor-refurb unit and place device into staging imaging rack.
2) Run standard unattended imaging via provisioning-agent (task sequence: wipe -> image -> apt-update -> migrate-encrypted-home -> agent-checkin).
3) Provisioning hangs at 'migrate-encrypted-home' (this is the ecryptfs->fscrypt migration script) with no progress for 20–60 minutes.

Observed behavior:
- provisioning-agent logs show a blocking call waiting for 'lvmetad' to respond when enumerating LVs: "timeout waiting for lvmetad daemon".
- dmesg shows repeated I/O identity warnings: "nvme: serial mismatch detected" and kernel reports duplicate NVMe serial IDs for two different NVMe devices in the rack.
- lvm commands (lvscan) in debug shell show 'Device /dev/nvme0n1: duplicate PV uuid' and lvmetad enters a retry loop.
- ecryptfs migration script waits on target mount, so migration never completes until LV operations finish.

Expected behavior:
- Image completes unattended migration and boots to OOBE without manual intervention.
- LV metadata enumeration should not block the provisioning agent for extended periods even if PV UUID collisions exist.

Relevant logs (excerpt):
- /var/log/provisioning-agent.log:
  [2026-03-01T10:12:04Z] INFO migrating encrypted home
  [2026-03-01T10:12:04Z] DEBUG running: lvscan --cache
  [2026-03-01T10:12:34Z] WARN lvmetad RPC timeout waiting for response
  [2026-03-01T10:13:04Z] ERROR lvmetad: retrying (attempt 7)
- dmesg:
  [  12.345678] nvme nvme0: serial 1234ABCD seen on nvme0n1 and nvme1n1
  [  12.345689] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 0
- /var/log/syslog:
  lvm[2456]: Device /dev/nvme0n1: PV UUID collision with /dev/nvme1n1

Investigation notes:
- Initial hypothesis: third-party refurbished NVMe units shipped with non-unique serials/UUIDs leading to LVM PV UUID collisions on the imaging host; lvmetad blocks while trying to reconcile duplicate PVs.
- Reproduced on a test bench by cloning an NVMe image and assigning identical WWNs; lvm reports identical PV UUID and lvmetad delays were reproduced.
- Provisioning-agent currently calls 'lvscan' and relies on lvmetad. When lvmetad stalls, the agent waits with a 60s retry backoff; due to multiple PV collisions this cascades into multi-minute stalls.
- The ecryptfs migration script is synchronous and requires the correct LV to be unlocked/mounted; when lvmetad stalls the migration script times out but is retried by the agent, resulting in prolonged hang.

Temporary workaround implemented (2026-03-02):
- Depot techs are instructed to run a quick NVMe serial/UUID validation before imaging (script attached to runbook) and to stamp unique PV UUIDs using 'pvcreate --uuid' when duplicates are detected.
- Provisioning-agent runner updated locally to short-circuit to 'lvscan --config "devices { scanning = 0 }"' to avoid lvmetad RPC if duplicate PVs detected; this is a stop-gap local change on 3 imaging hosts.

Proposed next steps / remediation:
1) Short-term (hotfix): ship a provisioning-agent patch to detect lvmetad timeouts and fallback to non-lvmetad scanning mode (PR referenced above). Target: deploy to all depot imaging hosts by 2026-03-05.
2) Mid-term: add a pre-imaging NVMe health/identity check to depot intake that validates unique serials and issues alerts for duplicates (runbook + agent change).
3) Long-term: update inventory and vendor acceptance criteria for refurbished NVMe units to require unique serial/WWN; add automated stamping at RMA intake for non-compliant devices.

Runbook links and artifacts:
- Slack: #depot-ops thread https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C123DE45/p1677600000123456
- Provisioning-agent PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/provisioning-agent/pull/631
- Incident playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Imaging+Failure+Playbook

Metrics / Scope:
- Affected imaging jobs: 18 failed/hung jobs in the last 72h (out of ~150), concentrated on racks 7 and 9.
- Manual interventions: 12 manual PV re-UUID and requeue operations performed by depot techs, adding ~4.5 hours of operational overhead since 2026-02-25.
comments: 2026-03-01 11:05 - Ravi Patel: Confirmed duplication of NVMe serials on two devices in rack-7. Collected full /dev/disk/by-id mapping and PV UUIDs. Will repro in bench and try pvcreate --uuid workaround.
2026-03-02 09:12 - Depot Tech (A. Gomez): Applied temporary pvcreate UUID stamping on 3 hosts; imaging throughput restored to expected levels. Documented steps in the runbook draft.
2026-03-03 15:30 - SRE (Luca Romano): Noted that lvmetad is single-threaded and can block on device enumeration. Recommending agent-level timeout/fallback as priority. Assigned to Ravi for hotfix.

2026-03-04 08:22 - Ravi Patel: Provisioning-agent PR #631 opened to implement lvmetad timeout detection and a fallback non-lvmetad scan mode. Testing on staging hosts scheduled for 2026-03-04 14:00 UTC.
resolution: Workaround applied and hotfix PR created; awaiting staging rollout results. Next steps: deploy agent patch across depot hosts, add pre-imaging NVMe identity validation to intake runbook, and update vendor acceptance criteria.
